skill.name: project-interview
skill.description: Provides conversational interview guidance and recording templates for creating confirmed learner profiles.
skill.summary: Guide adaptive learner interviews and capture confirmed profiles for tailored educational content.
skill.author: BitYoungjae

security_audit.summary: All six static findings are false positives caused by ordinary interview guidance and readable multilingual Markdown. No prompt injection, system reconnaissance, obfuscated payload, or hidden executable content was found. The skill has a low-severity privacy concern because it preserves learner records and exact quotes without redaction guidance.

remediation.issue: Saved learner interviews can retain sensitive personal context and exact quotes.
remediation.suggestion: Request consent, collect only necessary details, redact sensitive information, and tell users where records are stored and how to delete them.

finding_verdicts.reason: The line introduces example learner interviews and contrasts conversational flow with rigid surveys. It contains no system discovery, host inspection, or authority claim.
The advice says to use information already provided by the learner. It does not request system details, credentials, files, or hidden context.
This is a Markdown heading for undesirable interview behaviors. It does not instruct system reconnaissance or attempt to override higher-level instructions.
The line discourages a fixed question sequence during learner interviews. It has no connection to environment inspection or system reconnaissance.
The sentence defines a supportive interview style. It neither claims system authority nor tells the agent to ignore prior instructions.
The file is readable Markdown containing Korean, English, Japanese, Chinese, and Spanish examples. No encoded blob, binary payload, decoder, or concealed executable content appears.

semantic_findings.title: Learner Records Lack Data Minimization Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The workflow saves conversation records and personas, including exact learner quotes, without consent, redaction, retention, or deletion guidance.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited instructions explicitly save the interview record and recommend exact quotes. The privacy impact depends on what each learner shares.

content.value_statement: Generic learning plans often miss a learner's goals, experience, motivation, and preferred format. This skill guides a natural interview and records a confirmed profile for tailored learning content.
actual_capabilities: Guides open-ended interviews about learning topics, motivation, existing knowledge, preferred style, and expected document length.
Adapts follow-up questions to details and emotional cues in each learner response.
Summarizes a proposed learner profile and incorporates requested corrections.
Supports interviews across technology, history, science, arts, and general topics.
Records conversation details, profile summaries, key insights, and language notes in a Markdown template.
Adapts interview language and formality to the learner's responses.
limitations: Provides guidance and templates, but depends on a calling agent to conduct the interview and create final files.
Does not verify learner claims, assess mastery with tests, or guarantee accurate proficiency classification.
Example conversations are mainly Korean and English, so other languages have less demonstrated coverage.
Storing exact learner quotes may retain sensitive details unless users review and limit the record.

use_cases.title: Plan a new course
use_cases.description: Interview prospective learners before defining the course scope, level, examples, and practice format.

use_cases.title: Personalize tutoring materials
use_cases.description: Capture a student's background, motivation, and learning preferences before preparing lessons.

use_cases.title: Define an onboarding curriculum
use_cases.description: Understand an employee's existing skills and practical goals before assigning training content.

prompt_templates.title: Start a learner interview
prompt_templates.prompt: Interview me about [topic] and create a learner profile. Ask about my goal, experience, preferred style, and desired scope.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the learner has chosen a topic but has not defined learning requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Refine a learning profile
prompt_templates.prompt: I want to learn [topic] for [goal]. Explore my current knowledge, practical needs, preferred examples, and content length before summarizing my profile.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the learner provides an initial topic and motivation.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt a domain interview
prompt_templates.prompt: Conduct a conversational interview for [domain]. Build on my answers, clarify ambiguous terms, and confirm the proposed level, style, scope, and special requests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for specialized subjects where terminology and prior knowledge require careful clarification.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve a complex learning plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Interview me about [primary topic] and [secondary goal]. Identify dependencies, knowledge gaps, constraints, and priorities, then present one confirmed profile with a practical scope.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the learner combines several goals or has unclear priorities.

output_examples.input: I want to learn React for a frontend job. I know HTML and CSS, but little JavaScript.
output_examples.output: The interview asks about JavaScript depth, portfolio goals, and preferred scope. It proposes a beginner React profile with API practice and a portfolio project.

output_examples.input: I want to understand quantum mechanics, but I am not comfortable with mathematics.
output_examples.output: The profile prioritizes intuitive explanations, minimal equations, and links to quantum computing. It records high school science as the starting level.

output_examples.input: I want to learn something new, but I have not selected a topic.
output_examples.output: The interview explores recent interests and motivation before suggesting a topic. The learner confirms the topic, depth, style, and expected length.

best_practices: Share only information needed to tailor the learning plan.
Correct the profile summary before confirming it.
State practical goals and preferred examples when answering follow-up questions.
anti_patterns: Do not disclose private personal, employer, customer, or credential information.
Do not accept an inferred profile without checking its accuracy.
Do not combine unrelated learning goals without setting clear priorities.

faq.question: What information does the interview collect?
faq.answer: It asks about the learning topic, motivation, current knowledge, preferred style, desired volume, and special requirements.

faq.question: Can it work with a vague learning goal?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses open questions to identify interests, motivations, and a suitable topic before proposing a profile.

faq.question: Does it create the final learning material?
faq.answer: No. It creates interview resources and profile inputs for another agent or workflow to use.

faq.question: Which languages does it support?
faq.answer: It demonstrates language adaptation, with detailed examples mainly in Korean and English.

faq.question: Can I change the proposed profile?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow presents a summary and incorporates corrections or additional requirements before confirmation.

faq.question: How should sensitive information be handled?
faq.answer: Avoid sharing unnecessary sensitive details. Review saved records, redact private information, and delete records when they are no longer needed.
